Claude Haiku 5.5 Pricing: The 100,000-Token Threshold | ImportStatic

# Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing jumps fivefold at 100,001 prompt tokens

Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing has two tiers. One token past 100,000 and the same request costs five times more. What counts, and a Go calculator to check your own.

 Published Oct 8, 2026 8 min read By ImportStatic Editors 

On this page

1. Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing is two complete price lists
2. What the docs say counts as the prompt, and what they leave out
3. One token over, priced in Go
4. An agent loop crosses the line on turn 17
5. It's still cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on both sides
6. Common questions

Tested with Go 1.27.1 on darwin/arm64, standard library only; no API requests were sent

A request to Claude Haiku 5.5 with a 100,000-token prompt and 2,000 tokens of output costs $0.011. Add one token to the prompt and the same request costs $0.055. Nothing else changed; you crossed a line in the price list.

Anthropic released Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026, and as of October 8 it's available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS under the ID `claude-haiku-5-5` (`anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` on Bedrock). The headline is the price: $0.10 per million input tokens against $1 for Haiku 4.5. The catch is that the cheap rate is for "prompts up to 100,000 tokens", and the model takes prompts ten times that size. A Hacker News discussion of the release went back and forth on whether agent workloads can stay under the line and didn't settle it. So we did the arithmetic with a small Go program. We had no API key in this run, so nothing below was sent to the model: the prices come from Anthropic's documentation and the costs are computed from them.

## Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing is two complete price lists

The pricing page gives Haiku 5.5 two rows, one "for prompts up to 100,000 tokens" and one "for prompts over 100,000 tokens". Per million tokens:

| | Up to 100,000 | Over 100,000 | Haiku 4.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $0.10 | $0.50 | $1.00 |
| Output | $0.50 | $2.50 | $5.00 |
| Cache read | $0.01 | $0.05 | $0.10 |
| Cache write, 5 minutes | $0.125 | $0.625 | $1.25 |
| Cache write, 1 hour | $0.20 | $1.00 | $2.00 |
| Batch input / output | $0.05 / $0.25 | $0.25 / $1.25 | $0.50 / $2.50 |

Every rate in the second column is five times the first. That includes output, which is the part people miss: the length of what you send decides the price of what comes back.

This isn't a marginal bracket like income tax, where only the excess pays the higher rate. The row is chosen per prompt and applies to the whole request. It's also unique in the current lineup. For the other 1M-context models the same page says "A 900k-token request is billed at the same per-token rate as a 9k-token request", and it names Haiku 5.5 as the exception.

## What the docs say counts as the prompt, and what they leave out

"Prompt" is doing a lot of work in that table, and the documentation doesn't define it as a formula over the `usage` fields. Here's what it does say.

With prompt caching on, the input is split across `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens`. The context windows page is blunt about cached tokens: "prompt caching changes what you pay for those tokens, not whether they count." So we treat the prompt as the sum of all three, which is the reading where a 100,000-token cached prefix plus a 50-token question lands in the expensive tier. That's our reading, not a quoted rule. If your bill depends on it, check a real invoice against a request you know the size of.

Two more things move the line.

Haiku 5.5 uses the newer tokenizer, and the migration guide says the same text "produces approximately 30% more tokens" than on Haiku 4.5. If you know your prompt sizes in Haiku 4.5 tokens, the threshold isn't 100,000 for you. It's about 76,900.

And the pre-flight check is approximate. The token counting endpoint is free and takes the s

Claude Haiku 5.5: Benchmarks, Pricing & Agent Costs

# Claude Haiku 5.5: Benchmarks, API Pricing and Agent Costs

Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic’s fast hosted model for routing, extraction and coding subagents. Its low starting price makes frequent calls practical, but agent benchmarks show why effort, context length and the number of attempts belong in the budget. It accepts text and images, supports a one-million-token context, and generates up to 128K tokens per standard request.

Content reviewed: 2026-10-12

## Use cases

- Extract a fixed set of fields from documents and validate them before updating a record.
- Route routine requests, escalating ambiguous cases to a human or a stronger model.
- Run a bounded coding subtask with tests, then compare accepted patches and the full attempt cost.

## Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing changes above 100K input

For prompts of 100,000 tokens or fewer, the Claude API charges $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. Above 100,000 prompt tokens, the rates are $0.50 input and $2.50 output for the full request. Use the request’s input length to select the applicable rate.

For an uncached response with usage.input_tokens of 20,000 and usage.output_tokens of 2,000, Haiku 5.5 pricing gives $0.003: $0.002 for input and $0.001 for output. A request with 120,000 input and 10,000 output tokens costs $0.085 at the higher tier. Apply the rates to your actual returned usage; tool calls, retries and reasoning output belong in the complete workflow bill.

Haiku 5.5 uses the newer Claude tokenizer. Anthropic says the same text counts as approximately 30% more tokens than on Haiku 4.5. Recount your actual prompts before estimating migration savings, especially near the 100K boundary. Compare the amount you pay to finish the work rather than multiplying the old token total by the new starting price.

Standard API prices from Anthropic’s Haiku 5.5 guide, checked October 8, 2026. Request examples use assumed billed tokens; cache, effort, retries and tools affect the complete task cost.

| Prompt length | Input / million tokens | Output / million tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≤100K | $0.10 | $0.50 |
| >100K | $0.50 | $2.50 |

- Haiku token limits and tiered rates ↗

### Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock: prices and routing

AWS’s US East (N. Virginia) price list, checked October 8, quotes Global Standard at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens through 100K prompt tokens, and $0.50 / $2.50 for longer prompts. The non-Global rates are $0.11 / $0.55 and $0.55 / $2.75: a 10% premium. Global cache reads and five-minute writes start at $0.01 and $0.125 per million tokens; above 100K they cost $0.05 and $0.625. Non-Global cache rates also carry the premium.

For Global cross-Region inference on bedrock-runtime, select global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5 explicitly; the US, EU, AU and JP profiles use the corresponding prefix. Global routing is a choice, not an automatic default. For example, us-east-1 supports Global and geographic routing, but not direct In-Region inference for this model. AWS lists Standard only, so the Claude API Batch discount does not apply here. Model charges appear on the AWS bill under the provider through AWS Marketplace.

- AWS Haiku 5.5 routes, regions and supported tiers ↗
- AWS published US East pricing data ↗

### Cache reuse and Batch costs for Haiku 5.5

At the ≤100K prompt tier, cache reads cost $0.01 per million tokens, five-minute writes $0.125, and one-hour writes $0.20. Above 100K prompt tokens, the respective rates are $0.05, $0.625 and $1.00. Cache-write and cache-read usage have their own prices; do not count them again as ordinary uncached input.

Claude Code’s cache lifetime depends on billing and request type. Main-conversation requests within a Claude subscription use one hour by default; API-key, cloud-provider and usage-credit requests default to five minutes, with configurable TTL. results.title: Haiku 5.5 is cheaper per token, but your bill jumps | Claude Lab
results.author: Masaki Hirokawa
results.text:
Haiku 5.5 is cheaper per token, but your bill jumps | Claude Lab

# Haiku 5.5 is cheaper per token, but your bill jumps fivefold past about 77k Haiku 4.5 tokens

On the price sheet, Haiku 5.5 costs roughly a tenth of Haiku 4.5. But the same text becomes about 30% more tokens, and a prompt over 100k tokens is billed at five times the rate. Here is the boundary in Haiku 4.5 terms, a script I actually ran, and the changes that return a 400.

When I first read the Haiku 5.5 price sheet, input at $0.10 per million tokens, I assumed I had dropped a digit. Haiku 4.5 was $1.00, so I looked twice.

I had not misread it. But the same table has another row: any request whose input goes over 100,000 tokens is billed at five times that rate. Starting a migration with "it got cheaper" in my head felt like setting myself up for the opposite surprise, so I ran the numbers by hand first.

What I'd like to say up front is that the boundary is not 100k if you are counting in Haiku 4.5 tokens. It is about 77k, because the tokenizer changed.

## The official numbers (checked on October 13, 2026)

| Item | Haiku 4.5 | Haiku 5.5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-haiku-5-5` (no dated ID) |
| Input / output per MTok | $1 / $5 | $0.10 / $0.50 (input up to 100k) |
| Requests over 100k | Same rate | $0.50 / $2.50 (5x) |
| Cache read | $0.10 | $0.01 ($0.05 over 100k) |
| Context / max output | 200k / 64k | 1M / 128k |
| Tokens for the same text | baseline | about 30% more |

Two details are easy to miss. The 100k check counts cache reads and writes too, and it is applied per request, so a cache hit does not save you if the total goes over.

## Computing the boundary

I turned the official numbers into a function that takes the token count you were seeing on Haiku 4.5 and returns the cost on 5.5. The output below is from actually running this script. Nothing was sent to the API; it is arithmetic only.

```
"""Haiku 4.5 -> 5.5: 同じ呼び出しの1リクエスト単価を比べる（USD / 100万トークン）"""
INFLATE = 1.30            # 公式: 同じ文章が約30%多いトークンになる
P45 = dict(inp=1.00, out=5.00, cache=0.10)
P55_LO = dict(inp=0.10, out=0.50, cache=0.01)   # 入力全体が 100,000 以下
P55_HI = dict(inp=0.50, out=2.50, cache=0.05)   # 100,000 超（5倍）
THRESH = 100_000
 
def cost45(fresh, cached, out):
    p = P45
    return (fresh*p["inp"] + cached*p["cache"] + out*p["out"]) / 1e6
 
def cost55(fresh, cached, out):
    fresh, cached, out = fresh*INFLATE, cached*INFLATE, out*INFLATE
    # 判定は cache 読み書きを含む入力の合計
    p = P55_HI if (fresh + cached) > THRESH else P55_LO
    return (fresh*p["inp"] + cached*p["cache"] + out*p["out"]) / 1e6, p is P55_HI
 
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"{'4.5換算の入力':>12} {'4.5':>9} {'5.5':>9} {'比':>6}  段")
    for n in (10_000, 50_000, 70_000, 76_000, 77_000, 80_000, 120_000):
        a = cost45(n, 0, 1000)
        b, hi = cost55(n, 0, 1000)
        print(f"{n:>12,} {a:9.5f} {b:9.5f} {b/a:6.2f}  {'上段' if hi else '下段'}")
    print("境目(4.5換算):", f"{THRESH/INFLATE:,.0f}")
    # 境目をまたぐ前後で 5.5 自身の単価がどれだけ跳ねるか
    lo = cost55(76_900, 0, 1000)[0]; hi = cost55(77_000, 0, 1000)[0]
    print(f"76,900 -> 77,000 : {lo:.5f} -> {hi:.5f} ({hi/lo:.2f}倍)")
    # 同じ 90,000(4.5換算) をキャッシュ読み 60,000 + 新規 30,000 で送る場合
    print("cache込み 90,000:", f"4.5={cost45(30_000,60_000,1000):.5f}", f"5.5={cost55(30_000,60_000,1000)[0]:.5f}")
```

Output:

```
    4.5換算の入力       4.5       5.5      比  段
      10,000   0.01500   0.00195   0.13  下段
      50,000   0.05500   0.00715   0.13  下段
      70,000   0.07500   0.00975   0.13  下段
      76,000   0.08100   0.01053   0.13  下段
      77,000   0.08200   0.05330   0.65  上段
      80,000   0.08500   0.05525   0.65  上段
     120,000   0.12500   0.08125   0.65  上段
境目(4.5換算): 76,923
76,900 -> 77,000 : 0.01065 -> 0.05330 (5.01倍)
cache込み 90,000: 4.5=0.04100 5.5=0.02665
```

(The column labels are in Japanese: input in 4.5 terms, 4.5 cost, 5.5 cost, ratio, and lower/upper tier.)

- Even past the boundary, 5.5 stays chea

How Claude Haiku 5.5 Pricing Works — 100K Threshold & Caching

API PRICING GUIDE · VERIFIED OCTOBER 11, 2026

# Claude Haiku 5.5 Pricing

The complete cost guide for both prompt-length tiers, cache reads and writes, Amazon Bedrock, Batch API and regional inference—with worked examples you can audit.

## $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens—until the prompt exceeds 100K.

For prompts over 100,000 tokens, Haiku 5.5 rises to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens. The threshold is evaluated per request, not from your monthly token total.

## Two tiers, including cache pricing.

USD per one million tokens on the Claude Platform.

| Token category | Prompt ≤100K | Prompt >100K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $0.10 | $0.50 |
| Output | $0.50 | $2.50 |
| Cache read / hit | $0.01 | $0.05 |
| Cache write · 5 minutes | $0.125 | $0.625 |
| Cache write · 1 hour | $0.20 | $1.00 |

The short-prompt tier is one fifth of the long-prompt tier for each token category. Cache hits are one tenth of the tier’s base input rate.

Open the interactive calculator

## The threshold applies to each request.

It is not a monthly volume threshold.

### At or below 100K

- Input: $0.10 / MTok
- Output: $0.50 / MTok
- Cache read: $0.01 / MTok
- Best unit economics for short, high-volume work

### Over 100K

- Input: $0.50 / MTok
- Output: $2.50 / MTok
- Cache read: $0.05 / MTok
- Still lower list price than Haiku 4.5 at equal token counts

Boundary case:

Anthropic describes the lower tier as prompts “up to 100,000 tokens” and the higher tier as prompts “over 100,000 tokens.” Exactly 100,000 prompt tokens therefore remain in the lower tier.

## From tokens to dollars.

Standard global pricing, before any cache or Batch adjustments.

$0.0015

10K input + 1K output in the short tier: 10,000 × $0.10/MTok + 1,000 × $0.50/MTok.

$0.0200

100K input + 20K output in the short tier. At 1,000 requests, that is $20.

$0.2250

200K input + 50K output in the long tier. At 1,000 requests, that is $225.

`request cost = (input ÷ 1M × input rate) + (output ÷ 1M × output rate) + cache costs`

Multiply the request result by request volume. Add any paid server-side tool usage separately.

## Three settings can change the bill.

Pricing modifiers may stack, so model the full request configuration.

−50%

Batch API discount on input and output tokens for asynchronous processing.

0.1×

Haiku cache-hit multiplier versus the applicable base input rate.

1.1×

US-only inference multiplier for Claude 4.6 and later models; global routing uses standard pricing.

A five-minute cache write costs 1.25× the base input rate and a one-hour write costs 2×. Caching pays off when reused prompt content avoids repeated full-price input processing.

## Bedrock Global uses the base rate; Geo routing is 1.1×.

Amazon Bedrock bills Haiku 5.5 through AWS Marketplace. These figures are USD per one million tokens and were checked against AWS pricing data on October 11, 2026.

| Token category | Global ≤100K | US Geo ≤100K | Global >100K | US Geo >100K |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $0.10 | $0.11 | $0.50 | $0.55 |
| Output | $0.50 | $0.55 | $2.50 | $2.75 |
| Cache read | $0.01 | $0.011 | $0.05 | $0.055 |
| Cache write · 5 min | $0.125 | $0.1375 | $0.625 | $0.6875 |
| Cache write · 1 hour | $0.20 | $0.22 | $1.00 | $1.10 |

### Bedrock identifiers

- Base model: `anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`
- Global profile: `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`
- US Geo profile: `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`
- EU, AU and JP Geo profiles are also documented

### Current Bedrock constraints

- Standard service tier is supported
- Batch, Priority, Flex and Reserved are currently marked unsupported
- Messages, Converse and Invoke APIs are supported
- Charges appear under the model provider in AWS billing

Amazon Bedrock uses Bedrock model or inference-profile IDs and AWS-managed features. Claude Platform on AWS provides Anthropic’s native

results.author: Soufiane Bellahmar
results.text:
Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 / $0.50, a tenth of Haiku 4.5

# Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 / $0.50, a tenth of Haiku 4.5

Anthropic's new small model costs a tenth of the one it replaces, but it is the first current Claude model with a prompt-length price step. The same day, Sonnet 5.5's cache hit was halved.

 By Soufiane Bellahmar · Published October 7, 2026 · figures checked October 12, 2026 

 Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (API id `claude-haiku-5-5`) on October 7, 2026 at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0.50 per 1M output tokens, with cache hits at $0.01, for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. That is a tenth of Claude Haiku 4.5's $1.00 / $5.00. On our blended 3:1 ranking it sits at number 10 of the 79 currently available models we track. 

## The 100,000-token price step

 Haiku 5.5 is the only current Claude model with a prompt-length price step. Anthropic's pricing documentation says a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens, counting cache reads and cache writes, pays $0.50 input and $2.50 output per 1M tokens, five times the standard rate, and that the higher price applies to the whole request, even when part of the prompt is a cache hit. Cache hits above the line cost $0.05 per 1M. Every other current Claude model bills its full 1M-token window at one rate. 

| One request, 2,000 tokens out | Claude Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6 Luna |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 90,000 tokens in | $0.0100 | $0.0100 |
| 110,000 tokens in | $0.0600 | $0.0120 |

 Crossing the line raises one request about 6x. If your prompts sit near 100,000 tokens, trim them below it or route the long ones elsewhere. More on these rules in the hidden costs of LLM APIs. 

## What a month costs at list rates

| Model | 100M in + 20M out | Same, 90% cache hits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | $20.00 | $11.90 |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 | $200.00 | $119.00 |
| GPT-6 Luna | $20.00 | $11.90 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $400.00 | $229.00 |

 List rates for prompts under 100,000 tokens, no batch discount, cache writes not included. The Batch API takes 50% off input and output. GPT-6 Luna lists at the same $0.10 / $0.50 with a $0.01 cache hit (OpenAI's rate as last checked 2026-10-02), so on short prompts the two cost the same per token; see Claude Haiku 5.5 vs GPT-6 Luna. 

## Other rates worth knowing

- Cache writes: $0.125 per 1M for a 5-minute write and $0.20 for a 1-hour write under the line; $0.625 and $1 above it.
- Context and output: 1M-token context, up from 200K on Haiku 4.5, and 128K max output, up from 64K.
- Tokenizer: Haiku 5.5 uses the tokenizer introduced with Claude Opus 4.7, which Anthropic says produces about 30% more tokens for the same text than the one Haiku 4.5 uses. See Claude's new tokenizer and what it costs.
- Thinking: adaptive thinking is on by default, and Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with an adjustable effort setting (default `medium`), so you can trade quality against tokens spent.

## What Anthropic reports on capability

 Vendor-reported figures from Anthropic's launch page, on its own harness. Anthropic also says Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 on average. 

| Benchmark (Anthropic's figures) | Haiku 5.5 | Haiku 4.5 | GPT-6 Luna | Sonnet 5.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GDPval-AA v2.1 (Elo) | 1620 | 735 | 1437 | 1840 |
| OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) | 72.4% | 15.7% | 48.9% | 83.9% |
| Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 39.2% | 0.0% | 16.4% | 70.6% |

## Sonnet 5.5's cache hit was halved the same day

 With the launch, Anthropic cut prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 to $0.10 per 1M tokens, 5% of base input instead of 10%. Input, output and cache writes are unchanged. Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work (a vendor figure). The cut puts Sonnet 5.5's cache hit level with GPT-6.1 Sol's; see the updated Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol analysis.

results.text:
Claude Haiku 5.5: API ID, Pricing Tiers & Setup

# Claude Haiku 5.5

Anthropic Oct 7, 2026 Major release Active

Use claude-haiku-5-5 for high-volume classification, extraction and routing. Price each request by prompt length: crossing 100,000 input tokens raises both input and output rates. Check the examples and setup steps before estimating a batch.

## Choose this model for a task

Anthropic positions Haiku 5.5 for high-volume, latency-sensitive work, including classification, extraction, routing and subagent tasks. A useful first evaluation uses representative records with known answers, checks missing fields and wrong labels, and counts retries. Lower per-token prices alone do not establish the cheapest successful workflow.

### API identifier and first checks

`claude-haiku-5-5`

1. Confirm your account and platform can access this ID using the official Models API.

# Claude Haiku 5.5 Pricing: API Rates, Costs & Usage

Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing starts at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0.50 per 1M output tokens. See cache, long-context, batch, and real-world costs.

Written by Bhavyadeep

Reviewed by Priyanka Singh

Last updated: October 9, 2026

Table of Contents H2

#### TL;DR

- Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing starts at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0.50 per 1M output tokens for requests up to 100K tokens.
- Requests exceeding 100K tokens cost $0.50 per 1M input tokens and $2.50 per 1M output tokens.
- Cache reads cost $0.01 per 1M tokens, and 5-minute cache writes cost $0.125 per 1M tokens for requests with 100K tokens.
- The Claude Haiku 5.5 model offers a 1M tokens context window, can generate up to 128K output tokens, and uses adaptive thinking with an effort parameter.
- Haiku 5.5 is about 75% cheaper to operate than Haiku 4.5 on average, after accounting for pricing and tokenizer differences.
- Batch requests offer a 50% discount on input and output tokens. This makes Haiku 5.5 particularly attractive for high-volume workloads that don't require immediate responses.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is positioned as Anthropic’s smallest, fastest, and most cost-effective model for high-volume AI tasks. Its use cases include classification, extraction, summarization, routing, browsing, customer support, and subagents.

While the advertised price is low, the real costs depend on how long your prompt is, how much output there is, caching, and the type of processing you choose, standard or batch. Here’s what you should know before you build on Claude Haiku 5.5.

## Claude Haiku 5.5 Pricing At a Glance

Claude Haiku 5.5 offers two price levels based on prompt length. The lower prices apply to prompts up to 100K tokens, while those over 100K tokens cost more.

| Token type | Prompts up to 100K | Prompts over 100K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $0.10 / 1M | $0.50 / 1M |
| Cache reads | $0.01 / 1M | $0.05 / 1M |
| 5-minute cache writes | $0.125 / 1M | $0.625 / 1M |
| 1-hour cache writes | $0.20 / 1M | $1.00 / 1M |
| Output | $0.50 / 1M | $2.50 / 1M |

About 90 percent of input requests for Haiku 4.5 were in the low prompt-size bucket. With improvements to its tokenizer, Anthropic estimates that Haiku 5.5 is about 75% cheaper to operate than Haiku 4.5 on average, after accounting for pricing and tokenizer differences.

Thus, Haiku 5.5 is especially appealing for use cases involving tens or even millions of relatively small input requests.

## How Prompt Caching Changes Claude Haiku 5.5 Costs

Prompt caching can reduce the cost of repeatedly sending the same context.

For example, an application might repeatedly send:

- System instructions
- Product documentation
- Knowledge bases
- Policies
- Reference material
- Agent instructions

Instead of paying the full input price every time, cached content can be read at a substantially lower rate.

For prompts up to 100K tokens:

- Input: $0.10 per 1M tokens
- 5-minute cache write: $0.125 per 1M tokens
- 1-hour cache write: $0.20 per 1M tokens
- Cache read: $0.01 per 1M tokens

That means a cached token read costs only 10% of the standard input price. For applications that repeatedly reuse large blocks of context, caching can therefore have a meaningful effect on the final bill.

## The 100K Prompt Pricing Threshold

One of the most important details in Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing is the 100K-token threshold.

Requests with prompts up to 100K tokens receive the lowest rates. Once the prompt exceeds 100K tokens, the higher rate applies to the request. Anthropic lists the higher rates as $0.50 per 1M input tokens and $2.50 per 1M output tokens.

| Prompt size | Input price | Output price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up to 100K tokens | $0.10 / 1M | $0.50 / 1M |
| Over 100K tokens | $0.50 / 1M | $2.50 / 1M |

# What Is Claude Haiku 5.5?

What is Claude Haiku 5.5? Anthropic's Oct 7, 2026 model: $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens, 1M context, benchmarks, and changes from Haiku 4.5.

Ashley Innocent

8 October 2026

Apidog for Enterprise

On-Premises Deploy

SSO & RBAC

Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic’s smallest and fastest current model, released on October 7, 2026, with the API id `claude-haiku-5-5`. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100K tokens, and $0.50/$2.50 for prompts over 100K. In its launch post, Anthropic says it costs “around 75% less to run” than Haiku 4.5 on average, and calls it “our fastest model to date.” It’s also the first Haiku with an effort setting, and it brings a 1M-token context window.

Below: specs, the two-tier price, changes from Haiku 4.5, benchmarks, where to run it, and who should switch, with links to deeper guides like the Haiku 5.5 pricing breakdown. To call the model as you read, Apidog can send the Messages request, keep your key in an environment variable, and show the response next to its token usage.

## Claude Haiku 5.5 specs at a glance

| Spec | Claude Haiku 5.5 |
| --- | --- |
| Release date | October 7, 2026 |
| Model id (Claude API, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS) | `claude-haiku-5-5` (fixed id, no date suffix) |
| Model id (Amazon Bedrock) | `anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` |
| Context window | 1M tokens (Haiku 4.5: 200K) |
| Max output | 128K (Haiku 4.5: 64K); 300K on the Batch API with the `output-300k-2026-03-24` beta header |
| Thinking | Adaptive only |
| Effort levels | `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| Knowledge cutoff | June 2026 |
| Price per MTok, prompts up to 100K tokens | $0.10 input, $0.50 output |
| Price per MTok, prompts over 100K tokens | $0.50 input, $2.50 output |
| Retirement | Not sooner than October 7, 2027 |

## Where Haiku 5.5 sits in the Claude lineup

| Model | Input / output per MTok | Default effort | Latency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Fable 5.1 | $10 / $50 | high | Slower |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 / $20 | medium | Moderate |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $2 / $10 | high | Fast |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | $0.10 / $0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens | medium | Fastest |

All four share a 1M context window, 128K max output and a June 2026 cutoff. Anthropic built Haiku 5.5 “for high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, extraction, and routing,” plus summaries, live support, browser use and subagent work under Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5.

The speed claim has a footnote: fastest “at each model’s standard speed,” but slower than Opus in Fast Mode. Anthropic publishes no tokens-per-second figure.

## Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing

The price depends on prompt length. A prompt over 100,000 tokens pays the higher rate.

The “around 75% less” figure is an average: 90% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 for prompts up to 100K tokens, 50% cheaper above, with 90% of Haiku 4.5 requests under the threshold. It already nets out the new tokenizer, which produces about 30% more tokens for the same text.

US-only inference (`inference_geo`) costs 1.1x on every token category. The minimum cacheable prompt drops to 512 tokens, from 4,096 on Haiku 4.5.

Under 100K tokens, the list price matches GPT-6 Luna exactly ($0.10 input, $0.50 output, $0.01 cache read, $0.125 cache write). The thresholds differ: Luna’s surcharge starts above 272K input tokens. The Haiku 5.5 vs GPT-6 Luna comparison works through that gap, and the pricing guide has worked cost examples.

## What changed from Haiku 4.5

The context window grows fivefold, max output doubles, and you get effort control for the first time. The migration guide warns that code written for Haiku 4.5 can break. Five changes return a 400 error:

1. Manual thinking budgets.`thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}` fails. Use `{"type": "adaptive"}` with `output_config.effort`.
2. Sampling parameters. Remove `temperature`, `top_p`
